raw_response: Banks reported strong engagement and loyalty among card members, with American Express noting a 13% year-over-year growth in loans and card member receivables. While this growth was elevated compared to pre-pandemic levels, both companies expected it to moderate through 2024 while still growing faster than billings. Regarding credit performance, banks maintained best-in-class metrics attributed to high customer credit quality and robust risk management. Although write-off and delinquency rates continued to tick up as expected, they remained below pre-pandemic levels for American Express. Wells Fargo highlighted that its new card products were well-received, with over 2.4 million new accounts opened in 2024 and strong credit card spend growth of over $17 billion year-over-year, all while maintaining strict credit standards.
